symptom: `create association … comment 'text'` reports success and stores **no documentation**, and a `/** … */` doc comment before the statement is dropped too — so an association is the one domain-model element with no working way to document it on create. `mx check` passes (an undocumented association is valid), and `describe association` simply shows nothing
cause: Both halves sit upstream of the writer, which has emitted `Documentation` all along. (1) `mdl/visitor/visitor_association.go` never called `findDocCommentText(ctx)`, the way the entity and enumeration visitors do, so `stmt.Documentation` was always empty. (2) The **plain-CREATE** branches of `execCreateAssociation` built the `Association` / `CrossModuleAssociation` literal without a `Documentation` field at all — while the `OR MODIFY` branches a few lines above them *do* set it, which is what makes the field look wired when the file is read casually
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_associations.go` (`associationDocumentation`, both plain-CREATE literals, both OR MODIFY branches), `mdl/visitor/visitor_association.go`; tests `mdl/executor/cmd_associations_documentation_test.go`
insight: **A field set on the OR MODIFY path is not evidence it is set on the CREATE path** — the two construct the element separately and sit next to each other. Grep for the struct literal, not for the field name. This is also why `comment` was *kept* on `create association` when it was removed from entity/enumeration/module/microflow/nanoflow/rule: there the doc comment already worked so the dead option was redundant, but here **neither** spelling worked, and removing the option would have left nothing at all. Check both spellings before deciding whether an option is dead or load-bearing
